tooltip.fast-noteblocks.mod_enabled: Master switch for everything the mod does out in the world: the labels over note blocks and repeaters, scrolling to retune them, and the placement sequence. The Composer is not affected and its key still opens it with this off.
tooltip.fast-noteblocks.debug_commands: Adds three subcommands: /fastnoteblocks paste builds a run of chords you type out rather than a song, asciidiagram draws a region as text, and debugpaste colours a build by what laid each block. They appear and disappear from tab-completion as this moves, and refuse to run while it is off. The README has the syntax.
tooltip.fast-noteblocks.radial_focus_del: Ticks the center label must stay under the crosshair before its radial opens and accepts scrolling. 0 opens immediately.
tooltip.fast-noteblocks.repeater_control: Radial select shows a four-number diamond and lets either wheel direction confirm a hovered delay. Scroll uses one number with directional cycling.
tooltip.fast-noteblocks.invert_scroll: Makes wheel-down raise the selected pitch instead of wheel-up.
tooltip.fast-noteblocks.view_distance: Maximum distance at which note and repeater labels are shown.
tooltip.fast-noteblocks.interaction_dela: Extra ticks between tuning interactions. 0 restores the original maximum of one interaction per client tick.
tooltip.fast-noteblocks.wait_for_ack: Waits for the changed block state to return from the server before sending the next interaction. Safer on restrictive or laggy servers, but slower.
tooltip.fast-noteblocks.require_line_of_: Cancels tuning if another block obstructs the path from your eyes to the target block. Disabled by default.
tooltip.fast-noteblocks.sequence_enabled: Runs or pauses the placement sequence without resetting its position, which is remembered per song. Double-tap the sequence key to switch between running and paused.
tooltip.fast-noteblocks.sequencing_edit_: While a nonempty sequence is running, disables overlay editing and optionally blocks ordinary right-click changes to existing note blocks and repeaters. Sneak-placement and automatic tuning remain available.
tooltip.fast-noteblocks.select_harp_bloc: Whether harp notes stop for a block of their own when Select instruments is on. Off, a harp note is a single step and you place only the note block. On, it asks for grass or dirt like any other instrument.
tooltip.fast-noteblocks.chord_place_orde: The order the sequencer walks the notes of one chord, which is built two notes to a block of bus. 2 strips walks the top row then comes back along the bottom, which is what a hand carrying one stack does. Alternating crosses the bus at every note. Neither moves a note.
tooltip.fast-noteblocks.select_instrumen: Makes the block under a note a step of its own, since a note block takes its instrument from what it stands on. Each note waits for its instrument first: the tile lights up, the hotbar picks that block out, and a wrong block waits rather than counting.
tooltip.fast-noteblocks.auto_select_sequ: Selects a note block or repeater from your hotbar whenever the current sequence step changes, including manual scrolling.
option.fast-noteblocks.ultra_lane_start_: Ultra lane starts at the top
tooltip.fast-noteblocks.ultra_lane_start: Where an Ultra compact lane build puts the snake down. Off starts on the bottom floor and climbs; on starts at the top and works down, wanting clear ground below the origin rather than above. Not mirror images — a descent is the dearer turn, so a song can come out better one way round. At one floor they are the same build.
tooltip.fast-noteblocks.max_build_floors: Upper limit on how many floors a Compact cube build may stack. The layout picks whichever count comes out closest to a cube, so raising this shrinks the footprint of a long song and keeps more of it within earshot. Each floor is four blocks tall.
tooltip.fast-noteblocks.commands_per_tic: How fast the Place tracks button sends its setblock commands. Higher finishes a build far sooner and is usually fine in singleplayer, but a server may treat a high rate as command spam and disconnect you. The three slowest settings send one command every two, three or four ticks, which is the pace a strict server will tolerate. A build reaching past your loaded chunks pauses at the edge either way, and resumes when you walk to it.
tooltip.fast-noteblocks.midi_quantize_gr: Grid that Edit > Convert for Minecraft snaps note starts onto, so the gaps between them become whole repeater delays. Auto reads a grid from the song’s own spacing. This is a conversion setting, not an import one: importing never quantizes anything.
tooltip.fast-noteblocks.midi_instrument_: Where each imported track's note-block instrument comes from. The MIDI file reads its General MIDI program changes, so a bass track arrives as a bass and channel 10 arrives as drums. Track names adds a fallback for files that never send one: a track called "Lead Saw" becomes a bit, "Kick" becomes a bass drum. Always the default gives every track the instrument below, which is what imports did before this setting.
tooltip.fast-noteblocks.conversion_gap_p: Share of the closest note gaps the automatic convert grid may ignore when choosing its resolution. Without this, a single pair of notes closer together than the rest sets the grid, and therefore the tempo, for the whole song. Ignored notes are quantized onto the grid and shift slightly. 0 uses the strict smallest gap.
tooltip.fast-noteblocks.repeat_merge_tic: When converting for Minecraft, collapses a repeat of the same pitch that arrives within this many repeater ticks into the note before it. Songs that fake a sustain by re-triggering a note every tick are otherwise unbuildable, and force the whole song to be slowed down to fit them. 0 keeps every repeat.
tooltip.fast-noteblocks.midi_velocity_cu: Drops imported notes quieter than this MIDI velocity, on both MIDI and NBS import. Off by default, because a cutoff inside a file’s own range removes music rather than noise, and a fade-in loses its opening. Note blocks have no volume, so quiet notes still cost a block each — but that is a decision better made in the Composer, where you can see them.
tooltip.fast-noteblocks.chord_thin_targe: How many sounds a chord is cut down to by Select > Overloaded chords. A build places 30 at one instant and no more, so anything at or under 30 builds. Thinning never drops the last of a pitch or the last of an instrument, so the harmony and the set of instruments survive.
tooltip.fast-noteblocks.midi_ignore_perc: Skips MIDI channel 10, which is usually drums.
tooltip.fast-noteblocks.midi_default_ins: Instrument id used for imported tracks, such as HARP, BASS, BELL, FLUTE, or MUTE.
error.fast-noteblocks.sequence: Notes must be 0-24 and repeater delay groups must be 1d-64d.
tooltip.fast-noteblocks.nearby_overlays: Labels drawn over every block of these types within view distance, whether or not you are looking at one. Something to read, not to use — retuning a block is the interactive overlay below. Off leaves nearby blocks unlabelled.
tooltip.fast-noteblocks.interactive_over: The overlay on the block under your crosshair, which you can scroll to retune. This is what the overlay key turns on and off. It works whether or not nearby overlays are showing: with those off, you see and change the one block you are aiming at and nothing else.
Which block types the interactive overlay answers for. Narrow it to repeaters if scrolling note blocks by accident is the problem, or the other way about.
tooltip.fast-noteblocks.all_keys: Vanilla’s own key bindings screen, where every mod’s keys are listed together. The three above are the same bindings, shown here so you do not have to go looking.
tooltip.fast-noteblocks.composer_gui_sca: GUI scale for this mod’s own screens, separate from Minecraft’s. A piano roll wants pixels, and the scale that suits a hotbar rarely shows four bars of a song at once. Same as Minecraft leaves the game’s scale alone; anything else applies while one of these screens is open and is put back when you close to the world. The window clamps whatever will not fit.
